subject: Budget range validation — PayBridge monthly spend & procurement thresholds
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Gupta <amit.gupta@paybridge.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + budget validation (token volumes / $/1M targets)

Hi Amit — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the follow-ups I promised: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary use case: real-time payment notifications + enriched receipts (bounded generation).
- Current production usage: ~5M tokens/month today (mostly inference for notifications).
- Expected ramp: target 25M tokens/month within 2–3 months as feature adoption widens.
- Procurement constraint: anything > $50k/month triggers Procurement/Legal involvement per your note.

Cost assumptions we discussed (ballpark estimates — attached spreadsheet has detail):
- Hosted API (no commit): list/benchmark pricing (illustrative): $1,000 / 1M tokens (public list for high-capacity models)
- Hosted committed tiers (10–50M): target pricing range we typically see: $500–$800 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated / reserved capacity (predictable throughput + batching): $200–$400 / 1M tokens effective with the right commit and batching profiles
- Caching/prefix reuse: real apps often see 20–40% effective token reduction depending on hit rates — this reduces spend accordingly.

What I need from you to validate next steps:
1) Confirm expected monthly token band (Today / 3-month target / 12-month target). From our convo: 5M today -> 25M target (please confirm).
2) Confirm procurement threshold — you mentioned $50k/month. Is that the hard cutoff for involving procurement & legal?
3) Which variant are you leaning toward: keep on Hosted with a committed discount vs. evaluate Dedicated (we can model both).

Attached: high-level pricing model and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) that lays out timelines and milestone-based billing options.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send a short pricing band note (hosted vs dedicated) with monthly cost examples for 5M / 25M / 40M tokens.
- If procurement threshold is confirmed at $50k/month and your ramp crosses that, we’ll loop in Contracts/Procurement on the next sync.

Thanks — feel free to correct anything above.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Amit Gupta <amit.gupta@paybridge.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + budget validation (token volumes / $/1M targets)

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the spreadsheet. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Volume profile: 5M tokens/mo (prod) today, likely steady ramp to ~25M within 8–12 weeks as we enable the new receipts flow. We have a longer-term goal of ~40M in 3–6 months if adoption is strong.
2) Procurement: correct — anything that commits us to recurring spend above ~$50k/month will require formal procurement and legal reviews (PO + SOW).
3) Pricing questions: can you confirm the examples you’ll send showing both Hosted committed tiers and Dedicated effective rates? Also curious how you model caching savings — conservative vs optimistic assumptions.

We’d like a couple of quick examples: monthly spend for 5M, 25M, and 40M tokens under (A) hosted committed band and (B) dedicated with a 6–12 month commit. If one of those bands keeps us under $50k/mo at our 25M target, that would help expedite purchase.

Finally, please include any notes on on-ramps (trial credits, short-term burst options) — we may want a low-risk way to validate before committing.

Thanks — Amit
Amit Gupta
Head of Platform, PayBridge
amit.gupta@paybridge.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Gupta <amit.gupta@paybridge.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + budget validation (token volumes / $/1M targets)

Thanks Amit — below are concrete examples using conservative/typical assumptions. I’ll also attach an updated sheet (same filename) with per-token math so you can plug your exact hit rates.

Assumptions used (conservative):
- Caching/prefix reuse: 25% effective token reduction (conservative middle-of-road).
- Hosted committed pricing bands we can typically achieve with a 6–12 month commit: $500–$800 / 1M tokens.
- Dedicated / reserved effective rates (with predictable throughput + batching): $200–$400 / 1M tokens depending on utilization and commit.

Examples (after applying 25% caching):
A) 5M raw tokens -> 3.75M billable tokens
- Hosted (at $800 / 1M): 3.75 * $800 = $3,000 / month
- Hosted (at $500 / 1M): 3.75 * $500 = $1,875 / month
- Dedicated (at $300 / 1M): 3.75 * $300 = $1,125 / month

B) 25M raw tokens -> 18.75M billable tokens
- Hosted (at $800 / 1M): 18.75 * $800 = $15,000 / month
- Hosted (at $500 / 1M): 18.75 * $500 = $9,375 / month
- Dedicated (at $300 / 1M): 18.75 * $300 = $5,625 / month

C) 40M raw tokens -> 30M billable tokens
- Hosted (at $800 / 1M): 30 * $800 = $24,000 / month
- Hosted (at $500 / 1M): 30 * $500 = $15,000 / month
- Dedicated (at $300 / 1M): 30 * $300 = $9,000 / month

Interpretation for procurement: at your 25M target we’re in approximately $9k–$15k/mo (hosted committed) or $5.6k/mo (dedicated) under these conservative assumptions. That keeps the monthly spend comfortably under the $50k procurement threshold, which should simplify procurement. If you ramp to 40M and we see list-like hosted rates ($800/1M), you’re still under $50k/mo in these examples.

Notes / next steps:
- If you want a more aggressive caching assumption (35–40%), we’ll show an alternate column — that typically brings costs down further.
- If you plan to evaluate Dedicated, we can model a 6–12 month commit with a utilization profile and show the break-even point vs hosted. Dedicated usually makes sense above sustained 50M–100M billable tokens but depends on latency/guarantee needs.
- I’ve added a MAP link in the sheet; if procurement requirements are strict, we can propose a milestone-based PO that keeps near-term commitment below their $50k threshold while allowing a path to scale.

Would you like me to include Procurement/Legal in the next call, or should I keep those conversations until you confirm a preferred vendor-pricing option?

Best,
Marissa

From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@paybridge.com>

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + budget validation (token volumes / $/1M targets)

Marissa / Amit — quick procurement note from my side:

- Confirmed: PayBridge policy requires Procurement + Legal review for recurring commitments above $50k/month or for multi-year platform commitments. A short-term PO/SOW under $50k/month can be approved by my team without a full legal review, which accelerates timelines.
- We are likely to hit ~25M tokens in the next 2 months based on current rollout; finance has indicated a willingness to approve up to $30k/month in the first quarter with a follow-up review at the 90-day mark. Anything above that will trigger the standard procurement path.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Marissa — please provide a 90-day pilot proposal (MAP + estimate) that targets ~25M tokens/month and keeps initial committed spend in the $12k–$30k/month band. Include milestone KPIs and an opt-in path to a larger commitment if we hit adoption targets.
2) Amit — I’ll schedule a short procurement intake meeting next week if you want Procurement involved early — otherwise we can do the intake once the pilot proposal is submitted.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Lee
Senior Procurement Manager, PayBridge
sara.lee@paybridge.com
